name: Longships and Sagas: The Viking World
description: Raiders, traders and settlers from Scandinavia sailed to Britain, Russia, Iceland and North America, and left laws, poems and a few kings behind.

checkpoints.name: Gods, runes and old tales
checkpoints.note: Scandinavians honoured Odin, Thor and other Norse gods and carved runes long before the first raids. Their world of sea kings and monsters lived on in poems and stories told by later writers.

checkpoints.name: The raiders arrive
checkpoints.note: A raid on a monastery in 793 began the Viking Age. Fast longships carried fleets to England, France and Russia, where Kievan Rus grew, while Alfred the Great fought the invaders.

checkpoints.name: Settlers across the sea
checkpoints.note: Norse farmers settled Iceland and held their Althing, and Erik the Red led settlers to Greenland. His son Leif Erikson reached the coast of North America, and the kings of England took shape.

checkpoints.name: The Viking Age ends
checkpoints.note: Vikings left traces at L'Anse aux Meadows, and Norse guards served in Byzantium. Cnut ruled England, Denmark and Norway for a time, Harald Hardrada's death at Stamford Bridge in 1066 ended the age, and the Normans won at Hastings, as the Bayeux Tapestry shows.

checkpoints.name: Sagas and poems
checkpoints.note: In Iceland scribes wrote the old stories down, including the Poetic Edda. Through these books, written long after the raids, the world of the Vikings and their gods reached later readers.
